extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists and students interested in US information/psychological operations
extracted.subtask_short: documenting a US online influence operation
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedia-style description of Operation Earnest Voice (OEV), summarizing the program's purpose, operational statements, and the software procurement requirements that specify how online personas/sockpuppets should be created and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Operation Earnest Voice (OEV) is a psychological operation by the United States Central Command (CENTCOM) that uses sockpuppets to spread pro-American propaganda on targeted social networking services based outside of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the overall objective: influence foreign/regional audiences via online personas and social networks; frames the program as targeted at non-U.S. social networking platforms and foreign-language sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator and sockpuppet licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fifty user "operator" licenses, 10 sockpuppets controllable by each user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies scale and operator-to-sockpuppet ratios required by the procurement request (enables a single operator to manage multiple personas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sockpuppet background and cyber presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sockpuppets are to be "replete with background, history, supporting details, and cyber presences that are technically, culturally and geographically consistent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires deep, consistent persona construction (biographical detail, supporting online traces) to increase realism and reduce detection risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic origin plausibility for personas
rubrics_metrics.description: Sockpuppets are to "be able to appear to originate in nearly any part of the world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personas must be able to plausibly present a geographic origin appropriate to target audiences; ties into hosting/IP configuration and cultural consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure VPN and IP randomization
rubrics_metrics.description: A special secure VPN, allowing sockpuppets to appear to be posting from "randomly selected IP addresses," in order to "hide the existence of the operation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement to obfuscate origin via VPN/IP techniques to reduce traceability and detection of coordinated activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static IP addresses to manage persistent personas
rubrics_metrics.description: Fifty static IP addresses to enable government agencies to "manage their persistent online personas," with identities of government and enterprise organizations protected which will allow for different state agents to use the same sockpuppet, and easily switch between different sockpuppets to "look like ordinary users as opposed to one organization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines persistence (static IPs) with identity protection and multi-agent access to personas so they can be used interchangeably while appearing organic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographically distributed private servers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine private servers, "based on the geographic area of operations the customer is operating within and which allow a customer's online persona(s) to appear to originate from." These servers should use commercial hosting centers around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement to host personas on servers close to target geographies (using commercial hosts) to enhance geolocation plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposable virtual machine environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtual machine environments, deleted after each session termination, to avoid interaction with "any virus, worm, or malicious software."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security and hygiene measure: ephemeral VMs reduce persistent compromise and isolate sessions from malware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach regional audiences via multiple channels
rubrics_metrics.description: CENTCOM commander David Petraeus stated that Operation Earnest Voice would "reach [a country's] regional audiences through traditional media, as well as via Web sites and regional public-affairs blogging," as an effort to "counter extremist ideology and propaganda."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational principle: combine traditional media and regional online blogging to maximize outreach and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and amplify moderate voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Petraeus: "We bring out the moderate voices. We amplify those."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical guideline: identify local moderate actors and boost their visibility rather than only producing original content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect, flag, and engage on hostile content
rubrics_metrics.description: Petraeus: "We detect and we flag if there is adversary, hostile, corrosive content in some open-source Web forum, [and] we engage with the Web administrators to show that this violates Web site provider policies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational procedure: monitor open forums for hostile content, flag it, and coordinate with site administrators to enforce policies or remove content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative control over regional blogging
rubrics_metrics.description: Jim Mattis altered the program to have "regional blogging" fall under general CENTCOM public-affairs activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational/policy note indicating that responsibility and oversight for regional blogging can be moved under established public affairs channels rather than covert operations.
